name: React
subtitle: UI library
creator: Jordan Walke at Facebook
description: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces out of reusable components. You describe what the screen should look like for a given state, and React updates the page efficiently when that state changes. It only handles the view, so routing, data fetching and server rendering come from frameworks such as Next.js.

concepts.explanation: Functions that return a piece of UI.
Read-only inputs passed from a parent to a child.
Data local to a component; changing it re-renders.
useState, useEffect and friends add state and side effects.
React compares UI trees and applies the smallest DOM change.
Data flows down through props, events flow up through callbacks.
Render on the server with zero client JavaScript (via frameworks).

codeSamples.label: JSX

pairsWith.reason: Fast setup for a plain SPA

pros: Largest ecosystem and job market of any UI library
Its component model is an industry standard
React Native reuses the same skills on mobile
Neutral governance under the Linux Foundation
React Compiler 1.0 now handles memoization automatically
cons: Only a library, so you choose routing, data and build tools yourself
Hooks have pitfalls such as stale closures and effect dependencies
Frequent paradigm shifts: classes, then hooks, then Server Components
Heavier bundles than Svelte or Solid
